title: P18: stable peak learning rate with a final 20% cosine decay
description: P18: retain the 200-step linear warmup, hold pretraining LR at 1e-3 until 80% of the absolute wall-clock budget, then cosine-decay to 1e-4 over the final 20%. Longer exposure to peak-rate updates may learn proof features that the fixed downstream expert-iteration procedure can extend.
hypothesis: No earlier registration tests a stable peak-rate phase. Longer warmup (022), reduced residual initialization (020), and EMA handoff (025) all reduced downstream transfer, motivating a different optimization trajectory rather than more smoothing. Sustained peak-rate updates may resist early short-proof specialization and learn reusable features before a short consolidation phase. This is an unverified mechanism: it may instead increase noise or overfitting and leave too little time to settle. The schedule also increases integrated LR-scaled AdamW decay at unchanged WD=0.1, so this does not isolate update size from effective decay. Only downstream three-seed dev-transfer performance decides keep/discard.
expected_delta: Central prediction +5 to +20 dev-transfer theorems at true length >=7 versus incumbent 012 (exact mean 147.67; stored rounded mean 148), with plausible downside -50. No additional model or optimizer work per step: expect approximately 3000 updates in the unchanged 300-second pretraining cap, including about 240 seconds before decay and 60 seconds for decay. The 200-step warmup retains priority if unusually slow initialization reaches the decay window. Per-token inference cost is unchanged, but learned generation lengths can alter total runtime under the fixed 1200-second cap.

optimizer.name: adamw
optimizer.schedule: 200-step linear warmup; constant peak until wall-clock fraction 0.8; cosine decay to min_lr_frac over final 0.2
